A_target.statement:
Let $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ be [[Definition:Finite Set|finite sets]].
Then:
:$\displaystyle \card {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i} = \sum_{\O \mathop \ne S \mathop \subseteq \set {1, \ldots, n} } \paren {-1}^{\card S + 1} \card {\bigcap_{i \mathop \in S} A_i}$

B_source.statement:
Let $A_1, \ldots, A_n \subseteq U$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \chi_{\bigcup_i A_i} = 1 - \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {1 - \chi_{A_i} }$
where $\chi_A$ denotes the [[Definition:Characteristic Function of Set|characteristic function]] of $A$.

substitutions.the set union |union A_i|: the sum over the ground set of 1_{union A_i}
substitutions.cardinality of an intersection: sum of a product of indicators

derived.expanded product prod(1 - 1_{A_i}): the alternating sum of intersection terms

object_map.reformulation: Replace sets by their indicator functions, prove the pointwise algebraic identity, then sum over all elements.

validity_conditions: 1_{union A_i} = 1 - prod(1 - 1_{A_i}) holds pointwise for every element (each side is 0 or 1 and they agree).
Expanding the product gives an alternating sum of products 1_{A_{i1}}...1_{A_{ik}} = 1_{intersection}.
Summing over the ground set turns each indicator sum into a cardinality, yielding inclusion-exclusion.
proof_plan: Encode each $A_i$ by its [[Definition:Characteristic Function of Set|characteristic function]] $\chi_{A_i}$ on $U = \displaystyle \bigcup_i A_i$.

For $x \in U$, $\displaystyle \prod_i \paren {1 - \map {\chi_{A_i} } x} = 0$ {{iff}} $x \in A_i$ for some $i$.
Hence:
:$\displaystyle \chi_{\bigcup_i A_i} = 1 - \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {1 - \chi_{A_i} }$

Expanding the product, and using $\chi_A \chi_B = \chi_{A \cap B}$:
:$\displaystyle \chi_{\bigcup_i A_i} = \sum_{\O \mathop \ne S} \paren {-1}^{\card S + 1} \chi_{\bigcap_{i \mathop \in S} A_i}$

Summing over all $x \in U$, and using $\displaystyle \sum_x \map {\chi_A} x = \card A$, gives the [[Inclusion-Exclusion Principle]].
{{qed}}
